Effect of red ginseng as a dietary supplement on metabolic syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis

Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a pathologic condition characterized by the aggregation of various pathogenic factors including hypertension, hyperlipidemia, abdominal obesity, insulin resistance, etc. It is the potential inducement of hyperuricemia, atherosclerosis and other diseases. The pathophysiology of MetS has not yet been completely confirmed. It may occur due to excessive dietary intake, lack of exercise, medication usage, or genetic factors. The treatment of MetS emphasizes on lifestyle changes, and diet control and physical exercise are the main methods for the treatment of MetS. For dietary improvement, choosing herbs as dietary supplements is a growing trend to improve MetS symptoms. Red ginseng, the dried root and rhizome of Panax ginseng C.A.Mey. after steaming, is a kind of traditional herb that is widely used in Asian countries. Clinical studies showed that red ginseng has a significant effect on lowering blood sugar, blood lipids, and blood pressure, which may be related to its effect on the regulation of intestinal microecology or other function. At present, there are meta-analysis studies on ginseng in the treatment of MetS and other related diseases. However, how red ginseng could improve MetS as a dietary supplement has not been reported.

Red ginseng, the dried root and rhizome of Panax ginseng C.A.Mey. after steaming, is a kind of traditional herb that is widely used in Asian countries. Clinical studies showed that red ginseng has a significant effect on lowering blood sugar, blood lipids, and blood pressure, which may be related to its effect on the regulation of intestinal microecology or other function. At present, there are meta-analysis studies on ginseng in the treatment of MetS and other related diseases. However, how red ginseng could improve MetS as a dietary supplement has not been reported.
